title: Platform Assessment
description: The findings behind a PPA certification decision for one platform release. The certification level is an aggregate, but the framework requires every assurance dimension to remain separately recorded, so this is the evidence a later eVault or reputation engine can inspect rather than relying on the headline level. Stored in the reviewed platform’s eVault with a public ACL, alongside the PlatformAccreditation that cites it.

assessmentId.description: Stable id for this assessment; cited by the accreditation.

platformVersion.description: The release assessed. Assessment is per release, not per application.

frameworkVersion.description: Version of the certification framework applied. Its thresholds are policy parameters and change over time.

dimensions.description: One entry per assurance dimension in the framework, recorded independently: a strong result in one does not erase a weakness in another.

level.description: Highest certification level this answer satisfies; -1 blocks certification.

source.description: Whether the app derived this from verified evidence or a reviewer asserted it.

unverified.description: True when the answer relies on evidence the ecosystem cannot yet verify, such as eReputation signals.

actors.description: Every accountable human actor and the identity assurance held for them.

verifiedAttesters.description: Of those, how many attesters were themselves passport-verified.

overridden.description: True when a reviewer set this IAL by hand rather than accepting the derivation.

minimumIal.description: The weakest actor’s identity assurance, which is what gates the level.

computedLevel.description: Level implied by the weakest dimension and the identity floor. Null when no level is supportable.

limitingDimension.description: Dimension id that held the computed level down.

awardedLevel.description: What the reviewer actually awarded. Null on a denial.

overrideReason.description: Required whenever awardedLevel differs from computedLevel, so a divergence is always explained.
